prerequisites: Vocabulary: understanding and ability to use technical-scientific language, especially regarding physics and mathematics
Computer science: ability to use/learn basic tools and software for scientific calculation
Communication: knowing how to present concepts and information in oral, written and graphic form
Organizational: knowing how to organize activities throughout the day and plan a medium-term work/study plan
Cognitive: Fourier Transform, Signal Theory, Probability Theory
Skills: ability to define the connection between physical phenomena, their properties and their representation both mathematically and in graphic form

learning_outcomes.text: Know and evaluate the main cellular communication systems, starting from the first generation systems, up to providing some information on the future 6G systems.
Analyze the main simulation tools for mobile radio networks.
Know and understand the architecture (components and functionality) of mobile radio networks.
Know and understand the operating mechanisms of the modulation systems used.
Know and understand the main activities carried out for the design and management of a mobile radio network.
Be able to analyze the behavior of a mobile radio network.
Be able to identify the characteristics of a mobile radio network in order to design a part of it to meet the specifications.
Be able to use the methodologies to correctly configure a mobile radio network based on the characteristics of the channel.
Be able to apply the tools and criteria for the analysis of the properties of mobile radio networks.
Be able to define the parameters of a mobile radio network based on standard specifications.
Be able to design advanced digital telecommunication systems and understand the project specifications required for the creation of mobile radio networks and provide adequate solutions.
Know the main solutions currently existing for cellular networks in terms of network architecture, protocols, interfaces, procedures and management of radio resources.
Be able to organically illustrate the interdependence of the different modules that make up a mobile radio network.

Independently understand the technical documentation made available by the communities of telecommunication system manufacturers and by the main companies producing development software with particular reference to radio frequency systems for mobile radio networks.

syllabus_topics: Notes on radio propagation and fading
Selective fading in frequency and time
Rayleigh and Rice fading Digital modulations
Single carrier ASK, PSK, FSK, QAM, APSK, OQPSK, p/4 QPSK, CPM, MSK, GMSK
Multiple carrier OFDM Notes on radio access techniques, radio channel allocation, multiplexing and medium access techniques
Protocol with particular attention to GSM level 2 and level 3
GSM Handover, Location Update, Connection set-up, Data transmission and Rate adaptation
Quality of Service management in GPRS
UMTS protocol: physical layer, data link layer, network layer
Introduction to the concept of 5G systems
5G spectrum auctions and new use cases
Introduction to the concept of 6G systems
teaching_methods: Lectures with the support of graphic presentations
Exercises based on LabVIEW simulation software
Practical exercises on hardware systems (spectrum analyzers, signal generators, SDR card antennas)

assessment_methods.method: Projects carried out in progress (group work)
Oral exam (open-ended questions and numerical exercises)

assessment_rules: A series of projects will be assigned, to be carried out in groups and evaluated with a score of 10/30. The oral exam, consisting of open-ended questions and numerical exercises, will have a maximum score of 22/30. The final grade is the sum of the project score and the oral exam score, with a maximum possible score of 32. An overall score of 32 results in a grade of 30 cum laude.
